# GA-readiness assessment for Llama Stack

## Description

Systematically assess Llama Stack's readiness to graduate from Tech Preview to General
Availability. This investigation inventories the gaps between current TP quality and the GA
bar across four areas — API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and error handling — and
produces the definitive GA scope that the stability-hardening and support-posture work will
be scoped against. It also consolidates TP feedback currently scattered across support
tickets into a single triaged inventory. It resolves the strategy's open question: until
this assessment lands, the size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate.

## Scope

- Collect and triage Tech Preview feedback from support tickets into a single gap inventory.
- Assess API stability: the published API surface (LlamaStackDistribution CRD, the
  OpenAI-compatible REST APIs, provider plugins) against the GA stability bar.
- Assess upgrade paths: behavior and evidence for upgrading from recent TP releases.
- Assess scale limits: documented and validated operating limits.
- Assess error handling: coverage and quality against the GA bar.
- Classify every inventoried gap as GA-blocking or deferrable, with severity and evidence.
- Produce the definitive GA scope: the set of gaps that must close for graduation, sized so
  downstream hardening and support-posture work can be planned against it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the four assessment areas (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error
  handling), when the assessment completes, then each area has an inventory of gaps between
  current TP quality and the GA bar, each gap backed by evidence — measured by review of
  the assessment report, with no area left unassessed.
- Given TP feedback scattered across support tickets, when the assessment runs, then that
  feedback is collected and triaged into the gap inventory rather than left anecdotal —
  measured by traceability from inventory items back to their feedback sources.
- Given the inventoried gaps, when the GA scope is defined, then every gap is classified
  GA-blocking or deferrable and the stability and hardening work is sized — measured by a
  scope document the downstream hardening and support-posture work can consume directly.
- Given the completed assessment, when a reader examines it, then each area states current
  state, GA bar, and the delta — measured by a completed report covering all four areas.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): a GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and
  the GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), producing the
  definitive GA scope — this epic is the entirety of HLR-1.

# Llama Stack API stability guarantee and tested TP upgrade path

## Description

Put a stability guarantee on Llama Stack's published API surface so enterprise customers can
build production GenAI applications against it: explicitly versioned APIs, a published
deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases. The concrete
hardening scope is determined by the GA-readiness assessment's API-stability and
upgrade-path findings and the definitive GA scope it produces.

## Scope

- Introduce explicit API versioning for the published API surface (the LlamaStackDistribution
  CRD and the OpenAI-compatible REST API surface the distribution exposes).
- Author and publish a deprecation policy covering how APIs are deprecated and removed, and
  how consumers are notified.
- Implement and test the upgrade path from each of the last two TP releases to the GA
  release.
- Remediate the API-stability and upgrade-path gaps that the GA-readiness assessment
  classifies as GA-blocking.
- Incidental documentation touch-ups that fall out of these changes (updated references,
  examples, captions) are included here rather than split out.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the published API surface, when it is consumed, then the APIs are explicitly
  versioned and the versioning is documented — measured by inspection of the published API
  surface and its documentation.
- Given the deprecation policy, when a breaking API change is proposed, then the policy
  defines how deprecation and removal are communicated and timed — measured by a published
  policy document.
- Given a deployment on either of the last two TP releases, when upgrading to the GA
  release, then the upgrade path is exercised by test and documented — measured by upgrade
  test evidence covering both releases.
- Given the GA-readiness assessment's GA-blocking API-stability and upgrade-path gaps, when
  this epic completes, then each is remediated or explicitly re-classified as deferrable in
  the GA scope — measured by gap-by-gap traceability against the assessment.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): published API surface carries a stability guarantee — versioned APIs,
  deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases. Also carries
  the API-stability and upgrade-path remediation implied by HLR-1's definitive GA scope.

# Llama Stack production support posture

## Description

Establish the production support posture required for GA: documented SLO targets, a backport
policy, and a published supported configuration matrix. The content of the supported
configuration matrix and the SLO targets is scoped against the GA-readiness assessment's
scale-limit findings and the definitive GA scope.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the GA component.
- Define and document the backport policy: which releases receive fixes and for how long.
- Publish the supported configuration matrix covering the distribution's supported
  dependency configurations (the default vLLM inference provider; optional vector providers
  for RAG workflows), reflecting validated scale limits.
- Obtain sign-off from the support organization on the SLO targets and the backport policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the GA component, when a customer evaluates support, then SLO targets are documented
  — measured by a published SLO statement.
- Given a defect in a supported release, when it is fixed, then the backport policy
  determines which releases receive the fix — measured by a published backport policy.
- Given the supported configuration matrix, when a customer selects a configuration, then
  the matrix states whether that configuration is supported, consistent with the assessment's
  validated scale limits — measured by matrix coverage of the documented dependency set.
- Given the SLO targets and backport policy, when they are finalized, then the support
  organization has accepted them — measured by recorded sign-off.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P0): production support posture is in place — documented SLO targets, backport
  policy, and supported configuration matrix.

# TrustyAI guardrails as a supported Llama Stack safety provider

## Description

Make the TrustyAI guardrails integration with Llama Stack a supported, documented
integration from the TrustyAI side — moving it from an experimental integration to one the
TrustyAI team validates, documents, and commits to support in GA distributions. This is the
provider side of the integration; the Llama Stack distribution side (removing the
experimental flag and marking the integration supported there) is tracked separately by the
owning team.

## Scope

- Validate TrustyAI guardrails operating as the Llama Stack safety provider: exercise the
  integration end-to-end across the guardrails surface TrustyAI exposes.
- Identify and resolve compatibility gaps between TrustyAI's guardrails APIs and Llama
  Stack's safety provider expectations, or document supported workarounds.
- Document the supported configuration and integration steps on the TrustyAI side.
- Record the TrustyAI support commitment for the integration: what is supported and at what
  level.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a Llama Stack distribution configured to use TrustyAI guardrails, when
  guardrails-relevant requests are processed, then the integration operates as documented —
  measured by end-to-end validation evidence.
- Given compatibility validation, when gaps are found, then each is fixed or explicitly
  documented with a supported workaround — measured by gap-by-gap disposition.
- Given the TrustyAI side of the integration, when a customer configures it, then supported
  configuration and integration steps are documented — measured by published integration
  documentation.
- Given the completed validation, when the integration is proposed for supported status,
  then the TrustyAI team's support commitment for it is recorded — measured by a support
  statement covering the integration.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration —
  TrustyAI side (validation, compatibility, documentation, and support commitment).

# Promote TrustyAI guardrails to a supported integration in the Llama Stack distribution

## Description

Remove the experimental status of the TrustyAI guardrails integration in the Llama Stack
distribution: the safety provider configuration moves from an experimental flag to a
supported integration for GA distributions. This builds on the TrustyAI-side validation,
documentation, and support commitment for the guardrails integration, and makes the
distribution's support status reflect it.

## Scope

- Change the distribution's TrustyAI safety-provider configuration from experimental to
  supported for GA distributions.
- Remove or replace the experimental opt-in gate for the integration in the distribution
  configuration.
- Ensure distribution-level configuration defaults and references reflect the supported
  status of the integration.
- Verify the integration operates when enabled, and that distributions that do not
  configure guardrails are unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a GA Llama Stack distribution, when TrustyAI guardrails are configured, then the
  integration is available as a supported integration — not gated behind an experimental
  flag — measured by the distribution configuration and its documentation.
- Given a distribution that does not configure TrustyAI guardrails, when it is deployed,
  then it operates without regression — measured by deployment tests with the guardrails
  provider unconfigured.
- Given the TrustyAI-side validation and support commitment for the integration, when this
  epic completes, then the distribution's supported status for the integration is consistent
  with that commitment — measured by cross-check between the distribution's support claims
  and the TrustyAI-side support statement.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an
  experimental flag) for GA distributions — Llama Stack distribution side.

# Decomposition Summary: RHAISTRAT-9014 — Graduate Llama Stack to General Availability

## Overview

Llama Stack shipped as Tech Preview with strong adoption, but enterprise customers will not
build production GenAI applications on a TP component. Graduation to GA requires: a
GA-readiness assessment (the definitive GA scope is currently unknown), API stability
guarantees with a tested upgrade path, a production support posture, a supported (no longer
experimental) TrustyAI guardrails integration, Dashboard enablement by default for entitled
clusters, and a GA-standard documentation uplift with TP migration notes.

Triage: the strategy is **not** below threshold (three components, three owning teams, and a
genuine unknown — the GA scope — whose resolution changes downstream epic scope) and is
**not** docs-only (HLR-2/HLR-3/HLR-5 require code and configuration changes). Full
decomposition performed.

All three affected components (Llama Stack, TrustyAI, Dashboard) exist in
`.context/rhai-components.txt` and have architecture context files, and all are
Konflux-onboarded — this is a graduation of in-platform components, so no onboarding chain
(repo-onboarding / license-validation / konflux-onboarding) is generated.
